title: Tercer condicional y wish + past perfect

rule.title: Third conditional and regrets
rule.explanation:
El tercer condicional imagina un pasado diferente y su consecuencia, que tampoco pasó: «If» + past perfect, «would have» + participio:
- «If we had checked the files, this wouldn't have happened.»

En la consecuencia también podemos usar «could have» o «might have»:
- «If you'd told me, I could have helped.»
- «If we'd left earlier, we might have caught the train.»

Para lamentar algo del pasado, «wish» o «if only» + past perfect:
- «I wish I had stayed later.»
- «I wish I hadn't uploaded it in such a hurry.»
- «If only I'd listened to you!»

Cuidado con la contracción «'d»: en la parte del «if» y después de «wish» es «had» («If we'd known», «I wish I'd known»); en la consecuencia es «would» («we'd have stayed»).

Ojo: nunca «would» en la parte del «if» ni después de «wish» para el pasado: «If I had known» (no «If I would have known»), «I wish I had known» (no «I wish I would have known»).

rows: If + past perfect, would have + participio
If I had known, I would have come.
If you'd asked, I could have helped.
